# Unfortunately, biases

## 1. Primary interval censoring

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The primary event falls somewhere in a window $[0, w_P]$
- It need not be uniform, but a uniform primary is fair when the
  window is short
- Mix the delay over where in the window the event sat, a convolution
  on the CDF
- A uniform primary has closed forms; we are working on more analytical
  solutions
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-primary-censoring.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A timeline. The primary event sits at an unknown point tau
inside a blue window of width w_P, the secondary event is a single red
line, and the delay is f(t - tau) averaged over tau."}

$$
F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(t) = \int_{0}^{w_P} g(\tau)\, F(t - \tau)\, d\tau
$$

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from [How to serial interval?][hsi], labelled there for a
serial interval · maths after
[primarycensored](https://primarycensored.epinowcast.org/)
:::
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note}
Gamma, lognormal and Weibull against a uniform primary have closed
forms.
:::

[hsi]: https://samabbott.co.uk/how-to-serial-interval

## 2. Secondary interval censoring

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The secondary event is recorded to the day as well
- The probability of a daily bin is a difference of the
  primary-censored CDF
- It doubles as the probability mass function for daily discrete-time
  models
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-secondary-censoring.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The primary-censored delay density, with the daily bin from n
to n + w_S shaded red and labelled as the difference of the CDF at its
two edges."}

$$
\Pr\!\big(T \in [n, n + w_S]\big)
  = F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(n + w_S) - F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(n)
$$

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from [How to serial interval?][hsi]
:::
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note}
In the past this was often written as a double integral, which is
typically more complicated to evaluate.
:::

## 3. Right truncation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A pair enters the data only if the secondary event happened before
  the cutoff $C$
- Condition on being observed, so divide by the CDF at the horizon
- Short delays are over-represented early in an epidemic
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-truncation.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Five delays from one primary event. The three that end before
the cutoff C are drawn in red and observed, the two that end after it
are dashed and never seen, and the likelihood is divided by the CDF at
C minus P."}

$$
L^{\mathrm{RT}}
  = \frac{F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(n + w_S) - F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(n)}
         {F_{\mathrm{PEC}}(C - P)}
$$

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from [How to serial interval?][hsi]
:::
:::
::::

## A mean of 3.9 days instead of 5.9

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
- At a cutoff seven days after the primary events, and 5.3 days at
  fourteen

::: {.attribution}
`LogNormal(1.6, 0.6)` with daily windows, computed for this talk with
`CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22,
`scripts/delays-right-truncation.jl`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
![](../figures/delays-right-truncation.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Two panels. On the left, the delay distribution seen by day 7
and by day 14 sits well to the left of the true distribution. On the
right, the mean estimated delay rises from under 2 days towards the
true mean of 5.9 days as the cutoff moves away from now, passing 3.9
days at a cutoff of 7 and 5.3 days at a cutoff of 14."}
:::
::::
